title: Reading a Science Article II: Correlation vs. Causation & Data in Text
goal: Tell the difference between "two things happen together" and "one causes the other"; read a percentage, a described graph, or a statistic used inside an argument and judge whether it actually supports the claim built on top of it.

questions: Explain, in your own words, why ice cream sales and drowning deaths correlate without either one causing the other.
In the vitamin/heart-attack example, name the possible confounding variable(s).

Think question: the passage says this "hides inside far less obvious... claims." Why is an obvious example like ice cream/drowning actually more useful for learning the pattern than a realistic-but-murky one would be on its own?
